thread.title: Kayne West plugs Adidas ties during rambling meeting with Trump - MarketWatch

author: Robert Schroeder
title: Kayne West plugs Adidas ties during rambling meeting with Trump - MarketWatch

organizations.name: marketwatch getty images rapper kanye west

text:
Getty Images Kanye West stands as he speaks during Thursday’s meeting at the White House. Rapper and entrepreneur Kanye West plugged his ties to Adidas during a White House meeting with Donald Trump on Thursday, saying the president had given him the “heart” to partner up with the sneaker maker.
Wearing a “Make America Great Again” cap, West delivered what amounted to a 10-minute monologue in the Oval Office while Trump looked on, mostly in silence, at one of his highest-profile celebrity supporters. The White House said West would be there to discuss issues including manufacturing and prison reform.
“You gave me the heart to go to Adidas,” West told Trump. West and the company have collaborated on the Adidas Yeezy Boost line of sneakers. Speaking earlier this week on CNBC, Adidas ADS, -1.28% ADDYY, -0.63% Chief Executive Kasper Rørsted said the company is “extremely happy” with its relationship with West. In the same interview Rørsted said Adidas had “outgrown” competitor Nike NKE, -0.25% globally and in the U.S., but “there is no doubt that Nike is coming back.”
See Also Why talking about retirement makes millennials mad × West has collaborated with Nike, as well, but he severed ties with the company in 2013.
“There was something about when I put this hat on, it made me feel like Superman,” West told Trump.
“You made a Superman cape for me,” West said, speaking metaphorically.
He said his parents had separated so there was not “a lot of male energy in my home.”
Alluding to the Kardashian family, he added that he’d also married into “a family where, you know, there’s not a lot of male energy. It’s beautiful, though.”
West said he loved Trump’s 2016 presidential rival, Hillary Clinton, but added that the Democrat’s “I’m With her” Campaign slogan didn’t work for him. “ ‘I’m With Her’ just didn’t make me feel, as a guy that didn’t get to see my dad all the time, like a guy that could play catch with his son,” West said.
The rapper also discussed another proposal — a hydrogen-powered plane that West dubbed the iPlane One and said Apple AAPL, -0.86% would help develop.
“That was quite something,” Trump said when West finished.
Robert Schroeder Robert Schroeder is the White House reporter for MarketWatch. Follow him on Twitter @mktwrobs.
